## §01 GAME + CORE (loaded first by every agent)
game: single-player real-time tactics + social infiltration · PC · Unity · camera above street, never first person · exteriors only (interiors = timed off-screen actions; shops, bars and workshops are frontages) · multi-level exteriors: street 0, deck 9.43 m, sky concourse 24 m (sky rail platforms) · mission = 1 block, 8–12 min, live clock
fantasy: commander. The city carries out your plan without knowing it: turn ordinary people, time their small acts into one plan.
arc: one person → networks → districts. Every system adds to or tests that growth.
look: bright retro-future (pastel cream + peach stone, saturated enamel accents, lagoon water, coral transit, chrome; skyline of towers, rockets, planets). Optimistic surface, coercive underneath.
world (Sky, 2026-10-14): an alternate history, not a forecast: "a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago". Culture and style 1950s, technology centuries ahead ("robots have 1950's style, the trams etc, just the technology is super advanced"). Not "the 1950s imagining the year 2000". People wear the city's space-age couture, never 1950s period dress (§15 people).
- atomic power made energy, travel and building cheap (sky rail, skyports, towers, liners): everything physical is abundant.
- thinking machines and networks never came ("internet wasn't a thing"): no networked computing; robots are clockwork-smart and follow fixed routines; records are physical (microfilm, punch cards, pneumatic tubes, stamped forms). Information moves through people and paper, so people are the weak point: why the game is about suborning them (pillar subvert people; tiebreaker people > powers).
- the city fears disorder most: an abundant, orderly city runs on routine and paperwork; hence optimistic surface, coercive underneath.
- design test for every object: 1950s style, centuries-ahead technology (crossing signals float, markings need not be paint; brief 009).
- reads (rules unchanged): cameras are closed-circuit, watched by people · a watcher's log is a physical record that investigators pull · calls are voice between people (telephone, radio) · "networks" in the arc and transit = people and lines, never computers · "no AI at runtime", fight AI and AI chatter are build terms, not the world.
pillars (test):
- subvert people: does knowing more make a person cheaper, quieter or more loyal?
- orchestrate the city: does it open or close a window the player can see coming?
- live with it: will the player meet this choice again?
tiebreakers, in order: readable > rich · people > powers · systems > scripts (nothing hand-authored) · preparation > improvisation · commander > avatar · exteriors only
pace (Sky, 2026-10-15: "more realtime than strategy"): real-time play is the default; pause is a tool, not the mode. The tiebreakers stand: you still command from above and prepare before you act. Show the rules in the street, not in text (Sky, 2026-10-16: "It's the reading, it's too much"): the systems stay deep, the player reads them from people, rings, lines and locks (§10).
terms: Trail = campaign evidence from traceable acts, drives investigations · Alert 0–3 = security response now (routine, inquiry, search, lockdown) · security level S 0–4 = how hard a district answers an alarm (lax, routine, watchful, guarded, swarm): the response dial (§05) · Standing = Hero ↔ Menace per district: acts seen or found, a public fight once by opponent, and word of mouth between missions; starts leaning Hero (+2) · Heat = T + Menace, threshold schedules a fight · bravery (helped → Fighter) / resentment (coerced → Informer) · Talker = fear + resentment > bravery + loyalty, gives you up when questioned
house rules:
- build only against Keel's rulebook (each event: needs, changes, witnesses). Unknown = reject.
- no AI at runtime. Content generated at build time. Same orders → same result. Any run replays exactly from start state + orders.
- handoff = inputs · done-check · next owner.
- only Latch edits Unity scenes. Price paid runs before starting.
- escalate to Sky (via Aster) only: pillar change, new paid spend, release, destructive action, unresolved conflict.

## §02 LOOP + RESOURCES
mission: Watch → Learn → Turn → Time → Take → Fight → Inherit
campaign: turned people pay cash/arms/tips → turn more people (snowball). Contacts grow braver or bitter. T + Standing set pushback.
| resource | scope | drives | from |
| Cash | campaign | fees, debts, bribes, turning | sources (skimming clerk, bookmaker) |
| Arms | campaign | winning fights, arming joiners; how many of your people carry a gun this mission (one sidearm per point; the Enforcer's carbine is the cell's) | sources (quartermaster, hijack) |
| Assets | campaign | access, income, fight allies | Fixer, introductions |
| Time | mission | actions 3–62 s (a kill 3 s, a knockout 6 s); events don't wait | — |
| Trail | campaign | investigations; part of Heat | traceable acts: threats, visible payments, people hit by gunfire, people taken down (knockout +4, kill +6, charged when a report is confirmed or the victim gives a statement), missing persons (+2) |
| Alert 0–3 | mission | security response now | reports that land (a witness, a camera, a missed check-in, a missing person), found faults, shots |
| Security level S 0–4 | district | the response's size and speed | the district's base, its open cases, the mission (§05) |
| Standing | district | who agrees, crowd behaviour | acts seen or found, public fights, word of mouth (§04) |
rule: every order shows its full price before commit ($, time, T, A risk, who would see it). In real time: one line per way on the action panel, the move ring on the ground, Alt for the breakdown, the going-loud card (§10).
travel [S]: boarding a tram or sky rail is fast travel round the city: board at any stop or station, ride to any other on the network. Price = time only: wait for the next service + the ride, both from the timetable. No fare.
chain: Handover route A is itself a chain (watch café → clear Inez's debt → loop camera → coffee spill pulls guard → take Vale). Each person sees only their part; city investigates backward, link by link [S]. Later operations chain more links across a district [L].

## §03 CELL
| op | verbs | notes |
| Scout | Watch, Listen, Mislead | Watch reveals a routine, and a watcher's sight (its cone) and check-in marks; Listen reveals need and temperament; false tips send rivals away; fires as untrained |
| Fixer | Turn, Call | offer/pay/help/threaten; calls contacts in on cue; the face witnesses remember; fires as untrained |
| Tech | Loop, Reroute | blinds surveillance, misdirects patrols; tethered while holding; fires as untrained |
| Enforcer | Enter, Take, Takedown, Fire | the only op who knocks out or kills in silence (§06) and who carries Vale; carries the carbine |
all ops [S]: any op can carry a sidearm (one per Arms point) and Fire (§06). Every op can run (double-click, or G on a moving op) at 2.8 m/s, twice the walk, and is noticed (§05). Any op can carry a body (the Enforcer at the walk, 1.4 m/s; the others at 0.7 m/s), put it down (1 s), restrain a living one (8 s) and stash it (§05 bodies). Nobody runs while carrying Vale, a downed op or a body, while tethered or mid-action; nobody fires while running or carrying.
training: full cell. campaign: starts Fixer only; recruit the rest by turning people with the skill [S].

## §04 PEOPLE
person = routine + need + temperament + memory. Knowledge lowers price; standing decides who listens.
approaches (Inez, training) [B]:
| approach | requires | $ | time | T | leaves |
| Ask cold | — | 0 | 25 s | +1 | remembered refusal: later offers +$10,000, +1 T |
| Pay | routine known (Watch 20 s [S]; was 52 s [B]) | 70,000 | 50 s | +2 | traceable payment; neutral |
| Help (clear debt) | need known (Listen 42 s) | 40,000 | 50 s | +1 | gratitude; bravery can grow |
| Pressure | need known | 0 | 35 s | +3 | fear; resentment grows; can identify Fixer |
purse: pay + driver = 110,000 > 100,000; help + driver = 80,000 fits → learning buys the second route.
private [S] (Sky, 2026-10-16: "seeing someone being turned isn't a concern. That's too much, would consider the conversation private, unless it's pressure"): Ask, Pay, Help and Listen have no witnesses: onlookers learn nothing, so they add no witness Trail, no Standing, no incident and nothing told along ties. The approach's own price stands (its Trail, time and cash; Pay is still traceable money; a Loyal subject still reports an approach). Pressure is not private: a threat is seen, remembered and passed on.
temperament [S]:
| type | responds to | Hero | Menace |
| Idealist | Help; refuses bribes | volunteers free; bravery fast | refuses; may report |
| Mercenary | Pay | overcharges | discount; sells you to highest bidder |
| Fearful | Pressure | hesitates; needs Help ×2 | folds free |
| Loyal (institution) | trust over time | turns after repeated Help | reports any approach |
Hero and Menace campaigns turn different halves of the city = replay value.
bravery [S]: Informant → Helper → Accomplice (hides op, drives) → Fighter (joins armed). +1 step per job completed unexposed.
resentment [S]: Compliant → Resentful → Informer (sells a route → ambush scheduled later). +1 step per pressure or exposure.
talker [S]: questioned, a person gives up known facts if fear + resentment > bravery + loyalty (deterministic). Facts: saw the Fixer's face, saw the Enforcer's face (a witness of a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), knows cell car, saw where/when. A person who reported volunteers place and time. Brave helped contact lies → nothing or false lead.
scales [S]: every number reads as a word: bravery informant·helper·accomplice·fighter (0–3) · resentment compliant·resentful·informer (0–2) · fear calm·uneasy·afraid·terrified (0–3) · loyalty none·obliged·trusting·sworn (0–3). Loyalty in the talker test = loyalty to the cell, 0 at start; loyalty to an employer or the civic order is the Loyal temperament. Start: everyone 0, except Idealist bravery 1 (helper) and Fearful fear 1 (talks when questioned until helped).
wrong approach [S]: an approach that doesn't suit the temperament still works one step worse (one more Help, or a higher price; Keel sets the numbers); an approach the temperament refuses (Pay to an Idealist) fails and leaves a remembered refusal.
preview: an order always shows its price; whether it will work shows as "?" until Listen reveals the temperament (Sky, 2026-10-15: Watch gives where and when; Listen gives who they are).
needs [S]: one clear need per person from a closed list: debt · cash · housing · papers · kin · care · protection · advancement · secret. Each is met by Help or Pressure; a need that requires something (kin: a family tie; protection: a rival tie; advancement: work) is checked in the data. A met need is replaced between missions, drawn from the person's own stream (id + mission number); a turned contact tells it free in the debrief, anyone else needs Listen again.
ties [S]: family ≤ 4 · workmate ≤ 3 (same employer) · regular ≤ 3 out, 12 in (their routine stops at the unit while its staff are on shift) · debtor ≤ 2 owed, 6 in · rival ≤ 1 (same trade or employer); 1–8 per person, nobody isolated, nobody a hub. Introductions travel only along family, workmate and regular ties.
knowledge [S]: a person knows a fact only if they witnessed it (clear sightline within 13 m, §05) or were told it along a tie: face to face within 20 m, or by phone to a tie indoors (calls are voice, §01); a told fact is never told on. At the start nobody knows anything about the cell, and the cell is known by face only (no alias [L]). A keeper knows the needs of their workmates and regulars (§08 tips). Facts travel along ties, never opinion; the one feeling that travels is the word of a person the cell helped or harmed, between missions (standing, below).
restricted [S]: guards, patrol officers and investigators are Loyal or Mercenary; councillors, watchers, pawnbrokers and credit bureaux are never Idealist. Every trade and role carries ≥ 2 temperaments; no temperament over 60 % of a cast row; a unit of ≥ 3 staff carries ≥ 2.
between missions: promoted (new access) · arrested (lost unless freed) · introduces a friend (new contact) · comes home after a knockout and gives a statement (unless quieted) · grieves a found killing (a turned contact takes the saw-violence move; other family, lover and workmate ties fear +1) · worries for a missing person (those ties fear +1) · tells their ties how the cell treated them (standing). Debrief reports each with cause.
standing [S]: per district, an integer; Hero band at +3 or more, Menace band at −3 or less. Every district starts at +2, leaning Hero (Sky, 2026-10-16: "Hero is kinda the default, if you're not seen then everyone assumes you're good (it's that kinda world)"), one known kindness short of the band.
- in a mission only acts seen or found move it: −1 per seen incident of a threat (Pressure), violence, a drawn weapon, a takedown or a carry; −1 for a found killing, even unseen; a missing person 0.
- a public fight (city people within 30 m of any shot; it ends 30 s after the last shot, or with the final fight) moves it once, when it ends, by opponent: fired on the guard, patrol, officers or robots −1; fired first on rivals the district does not fear −1; broke rivals the district fears +1 (Sky: "a rival gang that has menace level authority is a +1"); anything else 0. How the public sees a mission's rivals is mission data (the Handover's: feared); a district default comes later, with the campaign.
- between missions, word of mouth (Sky: "if you help in a good way then can move to hero"): each person the cell Helped tells their ties (+1); each it Pressured or knocked out tells of the harm (−1); once per person, not per tie; helped and harmed counts as harmed; at most ±2 per district per mission. The word is a feeling, not a fact: no face, place or time, nothing for investigators.
- drift: a district nothing moved this mission moves 1 step back toward +2, from either side.
Hero: help people (their word), shield civilians, drive off feared rivals in public, free arrested locals. Menace: shoot in crowds, public threats, harm bystanders, fight the police, a killing found. An unseen threat moves Standing only through the victim's word. Neither end loses.
| | Hero | Menace |
| turning | slower, dearer, loyal | faster, cheaper, betrayal risk |
| crowds | join fights, hide ops | obey from fear, report, scatter under fire |
| fights | fewer; police hesitate in crowds | more often; harder |
| street | graffiti, cheering, free tips | wanted posters, averted eyes, empty pavements |

## §05 PRESSURE
urgency = scheduled events with reasons, never an arbitrary countdown. Each mission defines its closing event.
security: the door guard's routine (café stop pre-shift) [B] · every staff post (guards, patrol officers, watchers) checks in by voice every 90 s from the start of its shift, and at its end; a missed mark is a report that lands at the mark, Alert 1 [S] · cameras: fixed cones, blocked by roofs/parked vehicles, on a screen a person scans every 20 s [S] · the player sees a watcher's cone only once the Scout has watched it; a watcher not yet watched shows "?" and still sees you (§03, §10) [S] · patrol sweep, breaks to gunfire within 30 m [B] · the response comes by the dial (below); the district seals the level's seal time after the later of a confirmation at Alert ≥ 2 and the response on the street (2:25 at S1 and S2) [S].
rivals [B]: same target, own schedule. False tip: away 3:50. Gunfire: arrive within 16 s.
| A | security does | raised by |
| 0 routine | follows schedules | — |
| 1 inquiry [S] | robots check the spot; patrol tightens | a landed report of a found knockout, a woken victim, a noise, a missed check-in, a missing person; a found fault; once per incident |
| 2 search [B] | the response unit and robots to the place; the search opens stashes within 30 m | a 2nd incident; a landed report of a found kill or a carry seen; any gunfire at once (sets A ≥ 2; no per-shot +1 A) |
| 3 lockdown [B] | doors lock (S2 and up); cordon units at the district mouths; district seals | a landed report of a takedown seen; gunfire or violence seen by a civilian at once |
alert rule [S]: silent acts (a takedown, a carry, a body, a missing person) raise Alert when a report lands, never at sight; gunfire at once, because security hears it. Witness Trail and Standing still move at sight. A knockout found or woken never raises Alert above 1 (a takedown seen is 3 on landing, knockout or not). One takedown is one incident and one dispatch, however many find it.
witness [S]: clear sightline within 13 m of a traceable act → +1 T per incident, moves standing. Turning is private (§04): Ask, Pay, Help and Listen have no witnesses. A turned witness (loyalty ≥ 1) adds no witness Trail for a takedown or a carry and makes no report. Crowds also block guard/camera sightlines.
reports [S]: a fact reaches security only through a person (no networks, §01). Whoever notices a takedown, a carry or a body reacts by the first row that holds: (1) a person turned for this very act (the driver who brought the car): never its witness · (2) staff: radio from where they stand (lands in 5 s) · (3) kin of the victim (lover, family): report at once · (4) turned (loyalty ≥ 1): keep quiet · (5) an Informer: report · (6) terrified: flee, never report · (7) Loyal: report · (8) Idealist: walk over to check the body, then report · (9) Mercenary: keep quiet until Alert 2, then report · (10) Fearful: flee an act, avoid a body, tell a tie. A reporter walks to the nearest report point (a staffed door, or a call box: the world places them so every street point is within 40 m of one), running after an act and walking after a body, and calls (6 s); the report lands. A live camera's lands at its next scan + 3 s; a robot's in 4 s. A reporter taken down before the report lands drops it. Whoever quiets, avoids, flees or reports also tells one tie: face to face within 20 m, or by phone to a tie indoors. No Tech action cuts a call box.
bodies [S] (Sky, 2026-10-16: "civilians can see bodies. They don't disappear; the enforcer has to take them into a quiet place"): a person knocked out or killed stays where they fell until moved; kills are shown, not cut away. An open body is found by anyone within 13 m on a clear line and by watchers in their cones. Only a stash hides one: a container (5 s on the street, seen as a carry; holds 1) or a service door (10 s, off-screen; holds 3). A container is emptied on a round every 15:00, its time learnable by Watch, in the mission only. A knocked-out victim wakes after 2:00, staggers 4 s and reports the assault (Alert 1; his facts become leads); hidden, he calls out every 10 s, heard within 20 m; restrained, he is silent until freed. On landing: a found knockout 1, a found kill 2, a carry seen 2, a takedown seen 3. A found body, knocked out or killed, brings a unit of officers at any Alert and holds the scene: the door the body lies at and every door within 13 m in sight of it refuse Enter and any exit until the unit stands down (1:00 after the last alarm at Alert 1, 3:00 at Alert 2, never at Alert 3). A body moved before the unit arrives makes the report unfounded: Alert stays, no seal. At Alert ≥ 2 the unit's search opens every stash within 30 m (10 s each). Preparation earns the right to leave a body: with the camera looped and the patrol rerouted, nobody may find it in time (Sky).
suspicion [S] (Sky: a person who expects someone and finds them missing grows suspicious and can raise the alarm): a person due to meet a lover, family member or workmate at a stop they share (from routines, never authored) who is there without them raises a missing-person alarm after 20 s (Alert 1). A turned waiter says nothing; a person being Taken reports nothing.
response [S] (Sky: "it's easy to swarm the play area with robots if we need to temper the game play"): a dial, data per district and mission, not code. S = the district's base (data in the plan) + ⌊open cases ÷ 2⌋ (at most +2) + the mission's bonus. The Handover runs at S2.
| S | name | dispatch | Alert 1 sends | Alert ≥ 2 sends | +1 unit every | unit cap | seal | Alert 3 adds |
| 0 | lax | 20 s | 1 robot | 1 unit | — | 1 | 3:00 | — |
| 1 | routine | 12 s | 1 robot | 1 unit | — | 1 | 2:25 | — |
| 2 | watchful | 10 s | 2 robots | 1 unit + 2 robots | 40 s | 3 | 2:25 | +1 unit, doors lock |
| 3 | guarded | 8 s | 2 robots | 2 units + 2 robots | 30 s | 4 | 2:00 | +1 unit, doors lock |
| 4 | swarm | 6 s | 3 robots | 2 units + 4 robots | 20 s | 6 | 1:30 | +2 units, doors lock |
A unit is 2 officers; a robot is an armed patrol unit, and robots count against the 30-combatant cap. An alarm sends the response to the scene, then to where the missing person's post, car and close ties are meant to be now, then to the alarm-raiser's ties (up to 3 each); robots go only to places within 60 m of where they start. Fighting out is a last resort, not a route (Sky).
running [S]: a runner is noticed where an act would be: people with a clear line within 13 m, and the cones of the guard, patrol, live cameras, response unit and rivals. People remember where and when (and the Fixer's face if he ran): a lead, no T, no standing. Security that sees a runner counts a found fault: A ≥ 1, once per run; a guard who saw a runner no longer fights at your side. Running is free once a fight is on, the run is loud, or the op is under fire.
drawn weapon [S]: seen by security → A ≥ 2 and that watcher engages (reacts 2 s, then fires); seen by people within 13 m → one witnessed incident (+1 T, A ≥ 1), and they remember the face; unseen costs nothing.
alarm inside [S]: once A ≥ 2 the target's building hides them: Enter +30 s (Handover 38 → 68 s).
levels [S]: street, deck and sky concourse are all exterior. Sightlines and the 13 m run in 3D: a slab blocks sight straight up and down, an open edge does not. People change level only by stair, ramp, escalator or lift (time from the plan). Watchers stand per level; a station watcher covers its concourse.
watchers [S]: cameras and civic robots stand at key places on the district plan (stations, stops, gates, squares). Any op in a watcher's sightline is logged with place + time, act or no act. Once a Trail is open, investigators can pull the log: each sighting is a lead (place + time). Hot (Heat over threshold, Motive sets it) or Menace standing in the district: a sighting counts as a witness report (Alert table).
investigators [S][L]: on foot question ~every 20 s; cars move fast, stop to question; count rises with A and T. Pick civilians near last incident by sightline + distance, not luck. Useful answer = fact with place + time → go there, question again; ~60–90 s per hop.
visible: questioning icon, dotted line joining held leads, unit following it.
counters: keep moving (sightings go stale) · reach witness first (pay/reassure/threaten; threat adds fear) · Scout false tip · citizens block cars · break sightlines in a crowd.
output: findings → debrief Investigation state → next mission. Hero campaign: brave locals give false leads.

## §06 FIGHTS
fights measure preparation (arms, brave contacts, streets). Not a separate combat game: fast and real-time, Syndicate-like; a fight is short, lethal and decided by what you prepared.
frequency [S]: Heat = campaign T + Menace standing. Threshold crossed → fight event (raid, ambush, rival hit) in next mission. No dice.
The security level S (§05) is a separate axis: Heat brings fights to the cell; S makes a district watch harder.
size [S]: act I 3–6 hostiles · II 8–15 · III 20–30. Hard cap 30 simulated combatants; rest = background crowd (run/cheer only).
your side: cell + Accomplice/Fighter contacts + crowd joiners (Hero), armed up to Arms stock.
citizen actions: scatter (breaks sightlines, covers retreat) · block (lorry, stalled tram, crowd vs police vehicles) · join (bare-handed or armed) · vehicle strike (ram barricade or rigged vehicle; driver always jumps clear).
content line: civilians are never the payload; no coerced suicide attacks. Menace can be uglier (collateral, witnesses) but no civilian dies as the weapon.

The Enforcer, within 1.5 m, knocks a person out (6 s) or kills them (3 s), silently: no gunfire rule applies, no money. A target who sees him coming (or witnessed one of the cell's acts this mission) is aware: unarmed, he struggles (+3 s), screams (heard within 20 m) and holds the Enforcer's face; armed, the takedown fails and it is a fight. Not targets: the patrol robot and cameras (Reroute and Loop are their verbs). Vale: a kill fails the mission; a knockout is refused (use Take).

orders [S]: fire (until the target is down; holds aim 3 s if the line breaks; walking keeps firing at the walking rate, running cancels it) · cease · stance: hold (fires only when ordered), return (default on draw: fires at whoever fires on this op), at will (fires at any combatant in reach, nearest first) · panic: every armed op draws and goes to at will, only once a fight is on. Combatant = a final-fight hostile, or anyone who has fired on or aims at the cell; never a civilian, contact, Vale, or a guard or patrol that hasn't engaged, so only an explicit fire starts a loud run. cost [S]: per person, not per shot: +2 T per person hit (once), +2 T more if they go down (a dropped guard = 4 T). Shots in the final fight are untraced (no T, no A; Sky, 2026-10-15); shots before it count. Gunfire still calls the response unit, draws rivals in 16 s, breaks the patrol within 30 m, moves Menace if witnessed. Shooting a contact ends the relationship. Shooting the target = fail.
hostiles [S] (Pulse): advance to the nearest free cover point (made at build time) toward their objective (the getaway car in the final fight, else where they last saw the cell); engage when a foe is in effective reach. Crowds within 30 m of gunfire scatter.
downed: op at 0 = downed; carry (3 s; the carrier walks and doesn't fire) to the car, or captured → rescue mission.
civilians targetable: anyone can be targeted (takedown). Violence on a civilian seen by anyone → −1 Standing per incident, on top of the fight's own move (§04); a contact who witnesses it loses bravery and gains fear and resentment → some Informer, more Talkers. Fastest way to undo progress.

§01 GAME + CORE › house rules
house rules:
- build only against Keel's rulebook (each event: needs, changes, witnesses). Unknown = reject.
- no AI at runtime. Content generated at build time. Same orders → same result. Any run replays exactly from start state + orders.
- handoff = inputs · done-check · next owner.
- only Latch edits Unity scenes. Price paid runs before starting.
- escalate to Sky (via Aster) only: pillar change, new paid spend, release, destructive action, unresolved conflict.

Prove the rules small, then dress them › How it's built
The rules live apart from the engine. Everything that happens in the city (a guard leaving, a contact answering) is an event with its conditions, effects and witnesses.
Any run can be replayed exactly from its starting state and the player's orders.
Unity has to pass the same 28 scenarios as the top-down test before it's trusted.
One simulation engine. A Unity-free C# library: Unity runs it live, build tools run it headless. Fixed 10 Hz tick, integer state; a replay is the orders plus checksums.
Performance is judged by frame rate at play zoom, not by polygon counts. The target is 60 fps at 1080p on a 15-inch MacBook Air M4 (Mac16,13), the reference machine. It has no fan and a 10-core GPU, so it is measured warm, after several minutes of running, at play zoom with people, vehicles and the simulation in, by a perf harness in a development build. A mid-range PC (an RTX 3060-class GPU with a 6-core CPU) must also pass, as a check, not the bar.
